Dabrafenib shows a DIVERGENT transcriptional response across the four primary cell types.

The four cell types split into two groups:

GROUP 1 — CONSISTENT RESPONDERS (AoSMC, dermal fibroblasts, skeletal muscle myoblasts):
These three cell types show correlated transcriptional responses at both the gene level (Pearson r of log2FC vectors: 0.60–0.72) and pathway level (Pearson r of NES vectors: 0.75–0.79). They share activation of inflammatory signaling pathways (TNF-alpha/NF-kB, IL-6/JAK/STAT3, interferon gamma) and suppression of cell-cycle programs (E2F targets, G2-M checkpoint, mitotic spindle). Direction concordance when both cell types enrich a pathway: 94–100%.

GROUP 2 — DIVERGENT RESPONDERS (melanocytes):
Melanocytes are the clear outlier. Gene-level correlation with other cell types: r = 0.39–0.43. Pathway-level correlation: r = 0.23–0.28. Melanocytes show fewer activated DEGs (526 up vs 1,221–2,170 in others), lack inflammatory signaling activation entirely, and instead activate fatty acid metabolism, peroxisome, and protein secretion pathways. Only 606 DEGs (13.7–26% of each cell type's set) are shared by all four cell types. Only 1 Hallmark pathway (Unfolded Protein Response) is enriched in all four.

The divergence is consistent at both pooled all-concentration analysis and at the highest single dose (3000 nM), where melanocyte correlation with other cell types drops further (r = 0.28–0.37).

Interpretation: Melanocytes are the pharmacologically relevant target of dabrafenib (a BRAF inhibitor for melanoma). Their distinct transcriptional response likely reflects drug on-target effects in BRAF-driven cells, whereas the shared inflammatory/stress response in the other three cell types represents off-target effects in non-melanocytic tissues. This has implications for tissue-specific safety assessments: the off-target transcriptional signature in non-target cell types (AoSMC, DF, SkMM) is consistent with each other but differs fundamentally from the on-target response in melanocytes.
